web_evidence.title: The Paris Apartment: A Novel — Google Books
web_evidence.note: Publisher-permission preview metadata identifies the HarperCollins edition and displays a contents sequence rotating among named character sections; it corroborates the multi-voice structure but does not by itself establish grammatical person.

web_evidence.title: Lucy Foley Writing Styles in The Paris Apartment
web_evidence.note: Whole-book structural study explicitly states that the novel is told in first person by several narrators, including Mimi, Jess, Sophie, Nick, and the concierge, and describes each as contributing portions of the story.

web_evidence.title: The Paris Apartment by Lucy Foley, Review: Engrossing in audio
web_evidence.note: The review explicitly describes a multi-character revolving first-person narrative and alternating first-person narratives.

web_evidence.title: Book Review: THE PARIS APARTMENT by Lucy Foley
web_evidence.note: The review confirms that Jess, Nick, Mimi, Sophie, and other residents serve as recurring narrators and perspectives; combined with the diagnostic first-person passages, this corroborates multiple participating voices rather than a third-person frame.

person_note: The quotes repeatedly expose participating narration as I, me, my, we, and our across clearly different character histories, including Jess, Sophie, Nick, Mimi, and the concierge. Whole-book reviews and a Tier C guide describe rotating first-person narrators. Because multiple narrators remain in the same grammatical person, the correct label is FIRST, not ALTERNATING. Dialogue, proverbs, generic you, bare third-person references, and clipped fragments were not allowed to vote as contrary person evidence. Confidence is medium because no accessible Tier A/B prose or structural source establishes the complete configuration.
